_README: TEMPLATE for a new content type. Do not edit this file; it is the source
That creates config/types/articles.json and Articles-Pipeline/, and prints
what still has to be confirmed. Leading-underscore files are ignored by the
loader, so this one is never treated as a type.
EVERY value below marked CONFIRM is a guess until someone checks it against
the real export and the live Storyblok space. A wrong column name yields
empty fields silently rather than failing, which is the worst way to find
label: TYPE item

_comment: CONFIRM: where items of this type land.
`leaf` is the folder that holds the item. The tree AKU's front-end team
created carries news/, blogs/ and events/ at every level, so a type whose
leaf is one of those needs no new folders. A different leaf means asking
them for it -- the pipeline refuses to create anything under regions/ or
global/ and stops with instructions instead.
A type that does not use the full Region > Entity > Department depth can
drop patterns, or point several placements at the same shallower one.
CONFIRM: where this type lives on aku.edu -- the SOURCE, not the target.
These two are easy to conflate and are not the same thing. `hierarchy.leaf`
is where an item lands in Storyblok. This is where it came from: the path
SharePoint serves it under, the detail page its internal links point at, and
the shape of the id in those links (news_details.aspx?nid=NEWS-1234).
They coincide for news, which is exactly why the /news in build_link_map.py
went unnoticed. For blogs and events the values below are a GUESS -- check a
real internal link in the export before the first run, or every cross-link
will simply fail to resolve and be left pointing at aku.edu.
CONFIRM BEFORE THE FIRST UPLOAD: the component and its body whitelist.
news_article is the news component. A blog or an event may well have its
own, with different fields and a different set of allowed bloks. Reading
the live space is the only way to know:
python pipeline/fetch_storyblok_space.py
python pipeline/inventory_storyblok_components.py
The two asset ids are shared page furniture -- the background pattern
every article uses, and the backdrop behind every quote. If this type has
its own, replace them.
How source content maps onto components. These are the news values,
signed off against a reference story; see docs/PROJECT.md section 5.
spacing is NOT optional. Three values, chosen by component. A blok without
one renders with no vertical rhythm at all -- it is the single easiest
thing to get wrong and the hardest to spot in a payload.
CONFIRM: the source column names, from the real export.
These are the News list's names. A different list will not match, and a
name that does not exist produces an empty field rather than an error.
Check them against the export before the first full run:
python pipeline/new_type.py TYPE --check
`body` is the one that matters most -- get it wrong and every item is
blank. Add type-specific columns here too (a venue, a date range).
